subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported routing contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but this changes fallback routing, session ownership, provider/model selection, and permission boundaries, so repository policy treats it as a maintainer-owned product and security decision.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and redacted live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime fallback unchanged and add clearer doctor, status, and docs guidance for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Replace The Fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR only as source material after resolving its conflict, proof gap, diagnostics, and configured-agent guard concerns.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and redacted live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current evidence points to steipete across shared routing history, multi-account routing, and prior maintainer-facing review context for this contract decision.
